title: Several drivers given permission to start both races in Madrid
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of the FIA Formula 2 Qualifying session in Madrid, several drivers have lost their fastest laptimes and received permission to start both the Sprint and Feature Races in Madrid.

Firstly, Nico Varrone has lost his fastest time from Qualifying. The Van Amersfoort Racing driver was determined by the Stewards to have been the sole cause of the second Red Flag, a breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

With the deletion of his fastest time, was left without a time within 107%. In accordance with Article 34.2 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations, the VAR driver has been given permission to start both races from the back of the grid.

The Van Amersfoort driver is set to start the Sprint from 19th.

Secondly, Kush Maini has lost his quickest time from the session after being the sole cause of the first Red Flag, breaching Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.

As a result, the Indian driver was left without a laptime within 107%. In accordance with Article 34.2 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations, the ART Grand Prix driver has been given permission to start both the Sprint and Feature Races from the back of the grid.

The ART driver is set to start the Sprint from 20th on the grid.

Thirdly, Sebastiàn Montoya has been given permission to start both races in Madrid.

The PREMA Racing driver failed to set a time within 107%, however, as per Article 34.2 of the Sporting Regulations, has been permitted to start from the back of the grid.

Montoya is set to start the Sprint Race in Madrid from P21.

Finally, Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak has been given permission to start both races in Madrid.

The ART driver did not take part in Qualifying and subsequently had no time within 107%. As per Article 34.2, the Thai driver has been permitted to start both races from the back of the grid.

Inthraphuvasak is set to start from P22 on the Sprint Race grid.

title: Fittipaldi ready to capitalise on best F2 Qualifying result in Madrid
excerpt:
Emerson Fittipaldi secured P10 in the FIA Formula 2 Qualifying session in Madrid, a season-best result for the AIX Racing driver.

The Brazilian left it late in the day but kept his cool under pressure having had an earlier laptime deleted for exceeding track limits.

Reflecting on his session back in the paddock, Fittipaldi explained just how difficult the session was to manage from the cockpit.

"I'm very, very happy. I can only thank God for this result. It was a very stressful and chaotic qualifying as everybody saw.

"It's a very technical and difficult track and finally we got the car in the window where we could be competitive and in the top 10 and that's amazing.

"Because no one's been here before, I think that really helped level things out. Most of the other races this season, it was my first time there when all the others had already raced there, so that has been a big disadvantage.

"Today was very fair and the team managed to give me a very nice car and finally we have a top 10 and reverse pole tomorrow, so it's an amazing weekend already."

Diving deeper into his session, Fittipaldi explained how his qualifying session took shape, with the AIX driver losing an earlier effort to a track limits violation.

Along with that, the three Red Flag stoppages meant that there was no time to get into a rhythm during the half-hour session, and that it all came down to that final lap.

"Up until the last push of the whole qualifying session, I didn't have a lap in," Fittipaldi explained. "I was dead last, so it was very, very stressful. I got track limits and red flags here and there and you're like, 'oh my God, what am I going to do now?'

"Then in the last lap, I was like, let me give it everything I have and that was enough to put me in top 10, so that was good."

Looking ahead to the remainder of the Madrid weekend, Fittipaldi is aiming to capitalise on his strong grid position for both races.

Overtaking is set to be tricky according to the drivers, meaning that reverse grid pole potentially holds even more value around the Madring.

READ MORE

QUALIFYING: Beganovic storms to pole around Madring

The AIX driver isn't getting carried away however, and is focused on executing a clean weekend from here on out.

"Hoping for the best result possible. I don't want to add any extra pressure, just enjoy starting from the front row and do the best I can.

"I know that the team will give me the best car that they can do because the engineers have been working so hard this year and we've been working so much to try to develop and improve to be closer to the top teams. Finally, now we're getting there.

"I think it's going to happen mostly off the line, that's where most people are going to get their overtakes done. I'm in a pretty good position, I think, for tomorrow's race because it's a track where you really cannot overtake easily and it's very challenging.

"I'll just do the best race I can tomorrow and see where we finish."

title: Round 11 Post-Qualifying Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA FORMULA 2: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 2 Press Conference following Qualifying here in Madrid. Joining us in P3 from Invicta Racing, Rafael Câmara. In second place from Rodin Motorsport, Alexander Dunne; and from DAMS Lucas Oil, taking his third pole position in Formula 2, Dino Beganovic. Congratulations, Dino. How does that one feel?

DINO BEGANOVIC: It feels amazing to do it here in Madrid and to be the first one to do it here. Obviously, we did not get many laps in Free Practice, so that put a lot of emphasis on being well prepared for Qualifying through all the simulator work we did at the factory. I think we did a very good job. The car was really good today and DAMS did a great job to come back very strongly after a disappointing weekend last week in Monza. It feels very good.

FIA FORMULA 2: With the Free Practice running that you did have, how challenging was it to get the car properly set up for qualifying?

BEGANOVIC: I think the main thing is having trust between the engineer and the driver at that point, because the engineers cannot read much from the data and the drivers are still learning. You cannot learn much from an engineering perspective. My engineer and I dug into it a little and, in the end, we just tried to make me as comfortable as possible going into Qualifying. I think we did the right thing.

FIA FORMULA 2: This was the first Formula 2 Qualifying session here in Madrid. What did you make of the circuit?

BEGANOVIC: It is a crazy track. It brings the heart rate up very quickly, especially on a qualifying lap. It will also be very tough on the tyres in the races and physically hard on the drivers. I think we have some exciting races ahead, but tomorrow we will have to focus on gathering data for Sunday.

FIA FORMULA 2: Congratulations on pole position, Dino. Alex, congratulations on P2. Can you take us through your session?

ALEXANDER DUNNE: I think it was pretty good. It was a messy session because we had so many red flags, but one good thing for us was that we were at the front of the pit lane. We were first out, or one of the first out, each time, which is definitely useful in a qualifying session like this. I have qualified second and third many times, so pole would have been nice. But, considering how difficult the session was, I am pretty happy to have put together a clean lap and finished in the top three.

FIA FORMULA 2: Was it easy to get the tyre into the operating window, or did it take some coaxing to bring it in?

DUNNE: Today it was quite easy because of the red flags. We never really went out on a brand-new set and had the chance to build them up before pushing. We were always on fresh or used tyres, so they had already been through a heat cycle and were ready when we started to push. I did not even do a warm-up lap before my final lap and the tyre was already ready. If we had all gone out on new tyres after the final red flag, I imagine we would have struggled more, but because we had completed so many laps in between, it was not too bad.

FIA FORMULA 2: What are your initial thoughts on the track?

DUNNE: It is pretty cool. I had a few scary moments at the beginning of Free Practice, but it was much calmer and more relaxed in qualifying. It is definitely one of the more physical tracks. Of all the tracks I have driven so far in Formula 2, this will probably be the most physically demanding, and the Feature Race is a long one as well. I will need to make sure I am well prepared for that.

FIA FORMULA 2: Well done on P2, Alex. Rafa, congratulations, it looked like quite a final lap from you. What was it like in the car?

RAFAEL CÂMARA: It was not an easy Qualifying session. It was tricky to get the laps in, with a lot of red flags and crashes. I think there was one mistake on my side and, without that, the lap could have put us in a more comfortable position. I did not risk too much on the last lap, but overall I am happy with what we did today. In the end, it was a good lap that put us in P3. From here, we focus on the races.

FIA FORMULA 2: As I asked Dino, was it a challenge to get the car into a good setup window, or did you find it quite straightforward?

CÂMARA: It was not easy in Free Practice because we did not get many laps. It was difficult to get a read on what we needed to do for Qualifying, so you had to trust your engineer and the team to move in the right direction. Overall, it was a good Qualifying session without much data from Free Practice. That was the same for everyone, but on a new track it is not what you want. You want to have a good read and go into Qualifying knowing more about what is going to happen. It all came down to the final lap, which was very important because otherwise we would have been outside the top 10. We can be happy with what we did today.

FIA FORMULA 2: What are your initial thoughts on the track? Did you enjoy qualifying here?

CÂMARA: It is not an easy track, and it is quite easy to make a mistake, especially on a new circuit where there is not much grip or rubber. From a drivers' point of view, it is very nice. You need to be committed and confident on the lap. If you think too much about the mistakes you could make, you can end up making one. It was an intense qualifying session on a nice track.

title: QUALIFYING: Beganovic storms to pole around Madring
excerpt:
Dino Beganovic was in superb form to earn the Aramco Pole Position Award, his first since the opening round of the 2026 campaign.

The DAMS Lucas Oil driver was a consistent presence at the top of the times, delivering a 1:44.331 to take the first ever FIA Formula 2 pole in Madrid. He beat Alexander Dunne and Rafael Câmara to top spot.

On the first set of push laps, ART Grand Prix's Kush Maini suffered a spin ahead of Turn 15 and hit the wall to bring out the Red Flags.

In a separate incident, Sebastiàn Montoya tagged the barriers in his PREMA Racing car to sustain suspension damage. Maini was out of his car and OK while the Colombian recovered to pit lane entry.

The session resumed with 23 minutes remaining, and everyone eager to record a banker lap.

Nikola Tsolov was the early pacesetter, going quickest on a 1:46.328 for Campos Racing, with Dunne P2 for Rodin Motorsport, 0.002s down on the leading effort.

The second Red Flag arrived as Nico Varrone found the barrier at Turn 18 in the Van Amersfoort Racing #22. He was out of the car and OK, but everyone else returned to the pit lane while his car was recovered.

Running resumed with 18 minutes left on the clock and once again, there was a rush to get another lap in.

Dunne took top spot by almost a full second as the track continued to improve. TRIDENT's Laurens van Hoepen went up to P2 nearly eight tenths off top spot.

Beganovic then delivered a 1:45.182 to secure P1 by 0.2s over Dunne, with teammate Roman Bilinski going third-fastest with little over 11 minutes remaining.

The Swede found another chunk of time with eight minutes to go, setting a 1:44.578 to extend his advantage to eight-tenths of a second over his closest challenger in Dunne.

A third Red Flag arrived with just over five minutes remaining, with John Bennett in the barriers. The TRIDENT driver was OK, but his car needed clearing from Turn 11.

Running resumed once more with 05:28 on the clock and time for one last run.

Personal best sectors were flying in, and Dunne pipped Beganovic to take top spot briefly until the Swede finished his latest lap, lowering the time to beat to a 1:44.331.

Despite a big oversteer moment at the final corner, Invicta Racing's Câmara jumped up to third having been outside the top 10 prior to crossing the line.

Stenshorne and Tsolov set identical times, however with the Rodin driver completing his first, he lined up fourth ahead of the Championship leader.

There was one final incident, with Colton Herta spinning at Turn 19 into the barriers to leave everyone else unable to improve.

It left Roman Bilinski sixth ahead of van Hoepen, Noel León, Ritomo Miyata, with Emerson Fittipaldi completing the top 10.

The FIA Formula 2 Sprint Race is set to get underway on Saturday afternoon at 14:00 local time.

title: Nikola Tsolov: 'So far so good' after topping Madrid Practice
excerpt:
It was a positive start to the Madrid weekend for Nikola Tsolov, with the Championship leader topping Practice and what was FIA Formula 2's first session around the Madring.

The Campos Racing driver was consistently at or near the top of the timing sheets in what was a heavily impacted session following a Red Flag.

However, the Bulgarian driver was enthusiastic about his and the team's chances heading into the important Qualifying hour, and Tsolov says he is optimistic of a fight for pole.

"A very chaotic session, just like we were expecting. But I think I felt confident from the get-go in the car and confident with the track, so I was always there.

"It was all about putting the lap in at the right time, really. So I expect a lot to change for Qualifying obviously different compounds, but it's a good start and I'm happy with how we're working so far."

The Red Bull Junior Team driver also touched on Campos' preparation for the weekend, with the F2 team leaning on their F3 counterparts following a two-day test around the Madring last month.

Having data to analyse and compare to was hugely beneficial says Tsolov, who added that it meant the team wasn't starting from zero this weekend.

"F3 has been quite useful to us to check on-boards and obviously all the car-related stuff, set-up, bumps, all those things that are new to you when you jump in the car. At least you know some of those kinds of things.

"I think we've been working quite closely with the F3 team and that has been a benefit to us."

Looking ahead to Qualifying, the Campos driver said that the grid would encounter an entirely different track in terms of conditions.

The temperatures will be higher, while the switch to Soft tyres will give the drivers extra grip and confidence, which he believes could lead to further excursions as drivers find the limits.

"I think I'll take a similar approach. We expect a big jump in grip, so I'm definitely going to be pushing more in quali and then adapting to whatever the condition is in the session because as we saw, I think there's going to be a lot of offs and Red Flags probably.

PRACTICE: Tsolov tops Red-Flag affected Madrid opener

"The last couple of rounds haven't been easiest with penalties and things like that, so I'm just trying to get back on track as soon as we can.

"I've done the last three races with penalties consecutively. So, I'm trying to get back on track and quali is important here.

"Looking forward to having a bit more of a positive weekend and heading with better momentum into the final part of the year."

title: PRACTICE: Tsolov tops Red-Flag affected Madrid opener
excerpt:
Campos Racing’s Nikola Tsolov made a strong start to his Madrid weekend by topping the timesheets in Free Practice.

The Championship leader set the pace with a 1:47.059 to lead Van Amersfoort Racing duo Nico Varrone and Rafael Villagómez.

Tsolov was the early pacesetter on 1:50.065, but he soon found himself in P2 with Invicta Racing’s Joshua Duerksen going quickest by over six-tenths.

Kush Maini then took over at the top with a 1:49.120, but soon after his ART Grand Prix teammate Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak found the barrier at the exit of Turn 19.

The Thai driver was out of the car and ok. With the track cleared, running resumed with over six minutes to go after the session was extended.

Alexander Dunne went to P1 on a 1:48.286 with Dino Beganovic following him across the line to go to P2. The DAMS Lucas Oil driver was just 0.033s off the leading time.

Moments later, Tsolov returned to the top with a 1:48.245, before improving to a 1:47.059 on his next lap, with Nico Varrone 0.110s behind.

Maini briefly went quickest at the chequered flag but lost his time for exceeding track limits, just as Laurens van Hoepen found the barrier at Turn 13, bringing out the Yellow Flags at the session’s end.

Tsolov finished in P1 ahead of VAR duo of Varrone and Rafael Villagómez. Colton Herta was fourth ahead of Dunne, who made slight contact with the barrier at the final corner on his last lap.

Despite his off, van Hoepen was sixth ahead of Martinius Stenshorne with Oliver Goethe in P8 ahead of MP Motorsport teammate Gabriele Minì, as Rafael Câmara rounded out the top 10.

Many of the drivers had just one more lap before the session’s end and Tsolov improved to a 1:47.059. His nearest rival on this occasion was Nico Varrone, who was just 0.110s behind.

The drivers and teams will have a few hours to look things over before returning to the track for Qualifying at 15:00 local time later today.

title: PREVIEW: A new challenge awaits at the Madring
excerpt:
After the high-speed blasts around Monza, the FIA Formula 2 Championship rolls on into Madrid for a brand new challenge and one that will seriously test the teams and drivers.

The Madring is a fast street circuit with walls everywhere, ready to punish the smallest of mistakes should the ultimate limit be overstepped.

So with that in mind, here is all you need to know about the Spanish venue and Round 11 of the year.

WHAT TO EXPECT

Free Practice gets things started this weekend with Friday’s 45-minute session going green at 11:05 local time.

Qualifying follows later in the day, with the grid set for both the races at 15:00.

The first wheel-to-wheel action of the round gets going at 14:15 local time on Saturday, with the Sprint Race offering us our first glimpse of F2 racing around the Madring.

Sunday’s Feature Race brings what will surely be a thrilling round to a close, with lights out set for 11:25 local time.

STAT PACK

The Madring circuit runs to a total length of 5.414Km and features 22 corners, including the banked ‘La Monumental’ Turn 12 in Sector 2 as a highlight.

Madrid becomes the third Spanish venue after Barcelona and Valencia to host an FIA Formula 2 round.

Joshua Duerksen’s Feature Race win at Monza moves him level for the all-time wins record in F2 (8).

Rafael Câmara’s Monza Pole moves him level with George Russell, Oscar Piastri, Felipe Drugovich, Jack Doohan and Victor Martins with five apiece.

FROM THE GRID – Mari Boya, PREMA Racing

“It will be a big challenge for everyone because with the little amount of track time we have and it being a street track where no one’s driven before, preparation will be super important. “Arriving into Qualifying with the right setup and a clear idea driving-wise of what to do in every single corner will be tricky.

“I feel there are big fans of the sport in Madrid, so it will be really cool to have that support and I’m really excited about that.”

TECHNICAL PREVIEW

Pierre-Alain Michot, FIA Formula 2 Technical Director

“The Madring circuit will be a stern test for all of the drivers, with the walls all around the track never far away. Aerodynamic demand is high with the high-speed nature of the Madring, and tyre longevity will be a factor in the races. Those that take care of their Pirelli rubber will be rewarded.

“In terms of braking demand, the biggest stopping point will be at the Turn 5 chicane in the first sector of the lap. Overall, the narrow layout and demanding nature of the track will make Qualifying must-see.”

PIRELLI PREVIEW

Formula 2 cars will have the Hard and Soft compounds available for their debut at the Madring circuit. The choice therefore features a compound gap, aimed at accentuating the performance differential between the two options. In the Feature Race, the strategy that appears quickest on paper involves starting on the Soft and making a pit stop between laps 9 and 12. Temperatures could play a decisive role in stint management: in particularly hot conditions, the Hard could be prone to overheating, resulting in increased sliding and degradation. As this is a completely new circuit, a high likelihood of safety car interventions, as well as the possibility of red flags, can also be expected.

title: Racing in Madrid a ‘huge privilege’ says Boya as he previews upcoming weekend
excerpt:
Mari Boya is excited to get another chance to race at home as he previewed the upcoming weekend at the Madring

Mari Boya admits a victory in Madrid would be special although he is playing down expectations of what could be possible this weekend.

The PREMA Racing driver has endured a tough season to this point with just three points finishes so far in the campaign.

But as he prepares to race at home for the second time this year – after Round 5 in Barcelona – Boya, who was around for the Formula 3 test in Madrid last month, is excited to get back into the car.

“To be honest, it's a huge privilege to have two rounds in my country,” he said. “It's making it super special for me.

“Also because my family and friends are coming to watch. I feel a lot of support from them and also from the fans. I'm really excited to be racing again in Spain.

“It's a super challenging track. Not super long, but in terms of corners, it has many corners where you can make a lot of difference.

Boya is excited to get racing at his home race weekend in Madrid

“One of the trickiest things I think will be to close the lap because there are many corners so it’s difficult to get it right. Many combined braking zones, and kerbs that you need to use. So it's super challenging. It will be cool and challenging in qualifying especially.”

Boya’s P9 finish in Spa-Francorchamps Feature Race is his best result since Monaco, but there were signs of improvement for him and the team in Monza.

Chasing the Dream Season 8 Episode 11 – Out Today

The Spaniard narrowly missed out on a place in the top 10 in Qualifying and showed good pace in the races. He hopes it is a sign of what could be possible, especially as Madrid is a track where nobody has been before, meaning the drivers can make the difference.

“Maybe if you asked me this question last year, I would tell you yes,” said Boya on fighting at the front this weekend. “But I also know what it's like coming to a track with a new car and not being able to perform because of that. So tracks like this are super demanding.

“You also need the trust and the confidence from the car. Normally I really like street tracks and everything, but this year I discovered that I also suffer on them. I don't know to be honest what to expect.

Boya is hopeful of getting a chance at being on the podium this weekend

“But I am focused on myself. I have done the best job I could, came to the F3 test, gone twice to the simulator to prepare. I'm pushing myself a lot to be as prepared as possible and learning all the time.

“So let's see, we will discover when we go on track what we have.”

When asked if he has allowed himself to dream of a potential victory in Madrid, Boya responded: “To be honest, I'm trying to have the expectations where I feel they need to be.

“But winning at home is something special, and when you had the taste before of it makes you want it even more because you know how special it is looking under the podium at all the family, friends and also together with the team.

“That you are working together is something really beautiful, and Barcelona that year is a race that I will never forget.”

Next Up

title: WHAT TO WATCH FOR: The key items ahead of the Madring debut
excerpt:
We head back to Spain for Round 11 of the 2026 campaign but it is the capital of Madrid that hosts an FIA Formula 2 weekend for the very first time.

The Madring is a super-fast street circuit that will put the drivers to the test as they look to find the limit around the 5-kilometre layout.

Ahead of on-track action getting underway, here are a few key items you’ll want to keep in mind this weekend.

COMMITMENT REQUIRED

The Madring layout is a blend of flowing corners, blind entries and requires absolute commitment from the drivers in order to extract laptime.

Budapest’s middle sector with walls isn’t too far away from what the drivers will face. Of the races on the F1 and F2 calendar, the new Madrid track shares a few similarities with the Jeddah Corniche Circuit according to the Formula 3 drivers that have driven it during in-season testing last month.

With just one 45-minute Practice session to get to grips with the track ahead of Qualifying, those that are able to keep it clean and accumulate mileage will be at an advantage come the 30-minute grid-setting session.

As always around a street circuit, it’s about building up to the limit rather than finding it right away. Dial things in slowly, analyse where the time can be gained before going all out in Qualifying on Friday afternoon.

It will surely be a spectacle however, with the corners providing one of the most thrilling laps of the season in terms of man and machine working together in harmony.

Who will make history and secure the fastest time around the Madring?

LA MONUMENTAL

Fionn McLaughlin tackles Turn 12 during the F3 Madring test last month

Turn 12 is arguable the highlight of the new circuit, with a maximum of 13.5 degrees of banking, it is the most banked corner on the calendar and one that will thrill drivers and fans alike.

The right-hander is seemingly never ending, and rises as the drivers approach the exit of the corner into a tricky downhill braking zone for Turn 13.

It will compress the drivers into their cars as they get closer to corner exit, with the G-forces pushing them down into the cockpit before the rise over a brow of a hill and descending into sector three.

From there, the track really tests commitment, with a flowing series of lefts and rights to close the lap.

But that banked Turn 12 will be a spectacular place to watch from on the ground and will impress on TV too.

Will anyone be brave enough to try an overtake there? We will have to wait and see…

GETTING CLOSER IN THE TITLE RACE

Camara has been in great form and will be looking to continue closing the gap down to Tsolov

As things stand, Nikola Tsolov continues to lead the pack in the Drivers’ Championship, with six wins on the season putting him above the rest on 177 points.

However, with a fifth pole of the year and another Feature Race podium at Monza with P2, Rafael Câmara is slowly but surely chipping away at that advantage.

The points deficit heading into Madrid stands at just 11 points after the Invicta Racing driver’s podium around the Temple of Speed, and he is the driver in form currently.

In fact, the last time Câmara failed to finish inside the top four on a Sunday was way back in June at Round 4 in Monte Carlo.

Tsolov meanwhile hasn’t stood on the podium since his P3 finish in the Spa-Francorchamps Feature Race prior to the summer break, and has scored just 16 points in the subsequent two rounds compared to Câmara’s 41.

The Bulgarian driver will be aiming to curtail his rival’s impressive run of form this weekend, and re-establish himself as comfortable leader heading into Baku later in September.

title: John Bennett’s Monza Weekend Debrief
excerpt:
John Bennett delivers his verdict on what was an impressive weekend in Monza with another podium visit

It was a great Monza weekend for John Bennett as the TRIDENT driver secured one of his strongest finishes of the season in the Feature Race, ending up P4.

Reflecting on Round 10 overall, the Briton gave his thoughts on how he and TRIDENT were able to build into the weekend and maximise their result on Sunday.

BEST F2 WEEKEND TO DATE

"A really good weekend, by far my best Formula 2 weekend to date. Really strong throughout. We fell into a good place with the car from the start of the weekend. We met the top 10 goal in Qualifying and then I really feel like we maximised both races, I think.

“This weekend, the Invictas were just a little step above the rest of us. But P2 in the sprint, P4 in the feature from P10 on the grid, fighting up the field, it's been a really enjoyable weekend.

A WELL MANAGED RACE

Bennett was back on the F2 podium with a P2 finish in the Monza Sprint Race

“Talking through, the race itself. I think we managed all the phases of the race really quite well. You know, we had a decent lap one, and it came to me with the late battles.

“I think gained a position, and then settled into the race. I think we made the right call at the pit stop, pitting a lap earlier than most cars to get the undercut.

“The team did a great job on the strategy. We were really quick, managed to keep the DRS with León, and then passed quite a few cars coming out of the pits. Which was good.

READ MORE

Joshua Duerksen on ‘dream weekend’ and sweeping Monza

James Robinson heaps praise on Invicta drivers after Monza 1-2

"After the Safety Car restart, we were just then behind Dunne for the second half of the race and just reeling him in slowly. I felt quite a bit stronger than him, managed to make the pass. And then it was really tricky at the end.

“We had like five laps with no DRS. trying to hold off Dunne and Miyata behind. But, you know, we had the pace and the tyres to make it work. So I was just focused on getting clean exits making sure they couldn't attack me down into Turn 1 and we hung on for P4.”

CARRYING CONFIDENCE INTO MADRID

The TRIDENT driver is aiming to roll his momentum into Madrid and Baku

“For sure a really good confidence boost. You know, it's perfect coming back from the summer break.

“All the work I was doing over that period has paid off. Most of the work I've been doing throughout the year has been paying off. I’ve just got to say a massive thank you to the team.

“They worked super hard. The car's been really quick this weekend and it's been really quick all year. And they just keep on improving the car and they keep on improving me as a driver.

“It feels nice to finally get a decent points haul over the weekend, which is something that I think we've been very close to on a number of occasions, but it hasn't quite clicked for whatever reason. So, picking things back up with a really good weekend like this is really nice.

"This is a really strong weekend for me and the team. Madrid - no one's ever been there, so it'll be a bit of a challenge for all of us drivers and teams.

“I'm really looking forward to it. The track looks really, really fun to drive and it sounds really good from what I've heard from the F3 guys. But I’m looking forward to it and hopefully we can continue these results to the front of the field.”

Next Up

title: Joshua Duerksen on ‘dream weekend’ and sweeping Monza
excerpt:
It was a record-equaling weekend for Joshua Duerksen and one he dubbed one of his best of his career.

Sprint and Feature Race victory after missing out on pole by a tenth of a second to his teammate hauled him up to eighth in the Drivers’ Championship after a tough phase of the season.

Reflecting on his performance on Sunday, the Invicta Racing driver called it ‘a dream come true’ and said he was eager to earn the Formula 2 win record outright with a ninth victory before the end of the 2026 campaign.

"Incredible, really a dream come true. I think every driver could dream of a double win in Monza. I'm privileged enough to have this opportunity to say that I've won both races on the same weekend, just incredible really.

“The car was amazing, my pace was good, I felt good, so it's just an incredible race today. Eight wins now, right? That's really cool, I need to break that record. I want the ninth win. Maybe in Madrid, and then more in Baku as well.”

Diving into the race in more depth, Duerksen explained how tricky it was to control from the front, with the Safety Car wiping out his advantage.

He then had to contend with teammate Rafael Câmara in the closing stages, with the Brazilian following in his wheel tracks within DRS range.

Duerksen says that his performance and victories have boosted his confidence going into the rest of what is a busy month, and he is targeting more of the same in Madrid and Baku.

"It was quite tricky. Rafa and I were both very quick. I felt he had a little bit more pace than me on the Supersoft, that's why I boxed a bit earlier. Then my pace on the Softs was super strong.

READ MORE

James Robinson heaps praise on Invicta drivers after Monza 1-2

“I created a good gap where I could just pull away a bit or at least keep the same gap with Rafa. And then with the Safety Car, for sure not ideal, but I managed to have a very good restart where I managed to break the one-second gap, which then I could hold until the last four or five laps.

"Rafa was also very quick, and the guys from Invicta have done an amazing job, and I'm very proud of them. We had a very tough middle phase of the season. But I never stopped believing that I can do it, that I have the talent for it, or the capability.

“And I could finally show my true potential here in Monza. I think these are for sure some of my best races I would say, and I want to continue with this rhythm for the next races.”

title: James Robinson heaps praise on Invicta drivers after Monza 1-2
excerpt:
Invicta Racing enjoyed one of their finest weekends in FIA Formula 2, taking a 1-2 in Qualifying and converting that into Feature Race success on Sunday.

Joshua Duerksen led home teammate Rafael Câmara, a record-equaling win for the Paraguayan, as he achieved his eighth victory in the Championship.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, Invicta Racing Team Principal James Robinson was effusive in his praise for both drivers, paying tribute to Duerksen in particular after his impressive exploits around Monza.

"I’m feeling ecstatic,” he admitted. “It was a great job by the whole team today. I'm really, really happy for Joshua. He executed the race perfectly, he made a great start. He made the call to box on Lap 6, which was an aggressive call, especially with the risk of Safety Cars and obviously the potential for the overcut here.

“But he nailed the outlap and then controlled the race and was never really challenged. A massive credit as well to Rafa, who drove a very sensible race behind, didn't make any stupid moves, made the best race for the championship.

“But above all, I'm really happy for the team, for all the guys here who worked so, so hard. The engineering group, who always work well as a team, and the mechanic group as well, we always work as a team, we celebrate both sides of the garage.

Robinson was very happy with both drivers performances across the Monza weekend as they landed a 1-2 on Sunday

“To be able to celebrate the whole team as one is really special, because you don't get that very often in this job. So often in this world, one side of the garage is upset, you can't both have a great race normally. It's a very unique position to be in and I couldn't be happier.

Expanding on Duerksen’s improved form, Robinson explained that the Mercedes Development Driver took a while to adjust to his new team in 2026, but was now firing on all cylinders.

He added that the Paraguayan driver’s ability and mindset in the races had been particularly impressive, with his skillset on full display at Monza across the weekend.

READ MORE

FEATURE RACE: Duerksen goes back-to-back and sweeps Monza weekend

"I think this season has been a tough one. But this weekend, he's just shown exactly what he's all about. It took him a while to find his groove in the team. And I would say that cost him a lot of points early on in the championship. Just a few silly mistakes here and there, he really struggled to pull together an entire weekend.

“It's funny, that's what I said actually at the start of the weekend in the TV interview. And then he then goes and puts together the perfect weekend really. Only blemish was not taking pole position by half a tenth.

“So, his performance yesterday was arguably even more impressive than his performance today. But he's an incredibly intelligent driver. His understanding of the car is outstanding, and his ability to think strategically mid-race is really, really impressive.”

The Invicta team boss was full of praise for the team and their operations across the weekend as they claimed a big haul of points

Looking ahead to Madrid, the Invicta team boss says that the team is confident of rolling their good form on into Spain, but they won’t be looking at any title fight just yet.

The British outfit was able to close the gap down to leaders Campos Racing in the Teams’ Standings at Monza, with the gap down to 47 points.

Despite the positive weekend, Robinson says the team will be focused inward on continuing their form rather than eyeing up another big gain on the Championship leading team.

"Well, we never look at the points table. We only look at the points table at the end of the season. So, I have no idea what the gap is to Campos in the championship, but we just take every race as we can and do the best job. And if by the end of the season we can win both championships, that would be great.

“But I know that the gap to Campos is very big. So, we're not really looking at that at all. Obviously, Rafa is quite close now to solid in the Drivers’, I think that's much closer than the Teams’.

“But, we'll just keep doing the best we can each weekend, and not think about everybody else. We just think about what we do, control the controllables and what's in front of us. If we do that, then we can have a good weekend.”

title: Montoya penalised following Monza Feature Race
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of the FIA Formula 2 Monza Feature Race, Sebastian Montoya has received a time penalty.

The PREMA Racing driver was alleged to have caused a collision with Car 4 of Colton Herta on the approach to Turn 8.

After the race, the Stewards heard from both of the drivers involved along with team representatives and examined video evidence.

They determined that Car 11 had been wholly responsible for the contact as a result of a reactionary move rather than a defensive one. Consequently, the Stewards elected to apply a 10-second time penalty to the Colombian.

With the application of the time penalty, Montoya now finishes P18 in the final classification.

title: Round 10 Post Feature Race Press Conference
excerpt:
__FIA Formula 2: Welcome, everyone, to today's FIA Formula 2 press conference following a thrilling Feature Race here at Monza. Joining us in P3, from Campos Racing, is Noel León. In second place, from Invicta Racing, is Rafael Câmara. Also from Invicta Racing, he won the Sprint Race on Saturday and captured the Feature Race win today. It is his fourth win of the season: Joshua Duerksen. Now, Joshua, congratulations. You are the fifth driver in the modern era of Formula 2 to do the double. How does that one feel?

Joshua Duerksen: Really surreal. Just incredible. I feel like I am living a dream right now. Monza has always been very special to me. I have always felt very good here and, to be honest, this was a perfect weekend for me. I almost had pole position, missing out by just five hundredths, so for sure the pace was good. Then the Sprint Race victory and now the Feature Race victory have just been incredible. I am super happy with how the whole weekend went.

FIA Formula 2: It was very close between you and Rafa at the end there. How were you able to keep him behind you?

Duerksen: I was just doing qualifying laps every single lap. I know that Rafa is super quick as well, so I knew I had no margin for error. I was just pushing as hard as I could. The tyres were screaming; they were asking me to stop, but I just kept pushing. I think what helped me a lot was that, after the pit stop, I had a gap of more than one second. If Rafa had been within DRS, I think we would have been battling for the whole race: him overtaking me, me overtaking him, and so on until the last lap. So, yes, I think the initial pace on the Supersoft helped me a lot and allowed me to make it happen and get the victory today.

FIA Formula 2: Invicta Racing gave you both great cars this weekend. Can you talk about the job they have done?

Dürksen: Yes, Invicta Racing has done a very good job. They have given me a superb car all weekend long. We were quick in Free Practice, we were quick in qualifying and in the races. The car was just perfect. Having such a good car helps us a lot and allows us to extract the maximum from the tyres on every single lap.

FIA Formula 2: Rafa, coming to you next, congratulations. Take me through your race.

Rafael Câmara: Obviously, the start was not ideal, but it was okay. I got into P2 and, from there, I was just trying to hold the position. Obviously, I was hoping there would not be a Safety Car at the beginning because, for Joshua and me, after the Safety Car window it would have been a problem for one of us. But until then, it was quite okay. We were able to have a clean race. Then, with the pit stop, I think we lost a bit of time getting stuck with all the cars. But overall, I think it was a very good, very solid race after being a bit unlucky yesterday. It was good to score some strong points today. Obviously, I am very happy for Joshua and the team that we were able to finish P1 and P2 today.

FIA Formula 2: I saw you start to bridge that gap towards the end. Was it possible to try to make a move on Joshua at any point in the last few laps?

Câmara: Yes, I was really trying to get closer and at least attempt a move. Obviously, I wanted to win as well, but I think Joshua did a very good job today. He had very good pace and it was very close. So, huge congratulations to him. We will keep pushing. I think we have been making good progress. With every race, the whole team is getting stronger, and it is good to carry this momentum into Madrid.

FIA Formula 2: You picked up some really good points today. Just 11 points separate you from Nikola. What is it going to take for you to win this Drivers' Championship?

Câmara: I think, on that side, like I said before, I am just really focused on myself, trying to maximise what I can do and take the points. I think we did that very well today. Like I said, yesterday we were a bit unlucky, but we just need to keep this momentum. I think that, in the last five rounds, we have always been there and have always been consistent. We just need to keep doing our job. For sure, the fight is still open and we will keep pushing until the end. We never give up.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P2, Rafa. Noel, coming to you, congratulations on P3. That is your fifth podium of the season. Can you take me through your race?

Noel León: Yes, it was quite a good race, to be honest. We managed to do everything well and recovered some positions. It was unfortunate to receive that penalty from qualifying, which dropped us to P7, so finishing on the podium was the best possible outcome. These guys were just a bit too quick for me today. I tried to stay with them until the end, but they were quite fast over the final laps. I am very happy with the team, with the work it has been doing and, in general, with the whole weekend.

FIA Formula 2: Was it hard to manage the tyre in that final stint while trying to close the gap to Joshua and Rafa?

León: Yes, I think so. At the end, the degradation was not too high, so we were doing qualifying laps. I could not match them over the final three laps, so they started to create a gap. If they had been battling, I think I would have had a chance, but they never did. I am just happy with our result and with the weekend.

FIA Formula 2: Congratulations on P3.
